note: Step 1 Unity robot (2026-10-19). Body size and drive limits come from the shared robot.json named in paths; this file holds only the Unity-side details. Provisional simulation values, not measured, not tuned. After changing anything here or in robot.json, run the menu Warehouse Robot > Build Robot Prefab again.
conventions: Robot frame: +Z forward, +Y up (Unity, left-handed). v > 0 drives forward. omega > 0 turns left (counter-clockwise seen from above, REP-103 sign); Unity angularVelocity.y = -omega. pan_deg > 0 turns the pan camera left; pan 0 looks along the robot's forward axis. tilt_deg must be 0 (level camera, required by the lower-bound person distance). The 360 equirectangular image is world-aligned (RenderToCubemap renders world-axis faces): it does not rotate when the robot turns.
far_clip_note: far_m is a render distance only: v3 takes person distance from flat-floor geometry, not from rendered depth, so far_m must reach the whole warehouse (otherwise distant walls and the ceiling render as skybox). Checked at Play against the scene diagonal (RobotRig). Changed 2026-10-19 after the first Unity test: pan-tilt 10 -> 100 m, 360 50 -> 100 m. The 10 m far plane belongs to the THUD++ data only.

placement.note: On Play the robot is set onto the nearest surface tagged floor_tag below it (raycast from ray_start_above_m above its pivot).

collisions.note: Contacts with objects tagged ignore_tags are ignored by physics and not recorded. Touching the same object again within merge_recontact_s of losing contact counts as the same collision.

obstacles.note: Applied at Play by ColliderSetup, never to the vendored warehouse files: every direct child of a group object that has no collider gets a BoxCollider per mesh, and Rigidbodies under the groups become kinematic so the robot is blocked instead of pushing boxes and rack legs away.
